### Prerequisite

Load the `campsismod` package:

```{r echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(campsismod)
```

### The Structured JSON Format (v2.0)

Campsismod supports a structured JSON file format tagged with `"version": "2.0"`. Unlike the legacy format (version 1.0) which relies on raw text code blocks, version 2.0 uses an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) to explicitly structure equations, ODEs, compartments, and error models.

Furthermore, compartment names in v2.0 JSON files drop the legacy `A_` prefix (e.g., `ABS` instead of `A_ABS`, and `CENTRAL` instead of `A_CENTRAL`). Structural compartment attributes (`f`, `init`, `lag`, `duration`, `rate`) use these clean, un-prefixed names as keys.

Here is an example of a v2.0 JSON model structure:

```json
{
  "version": "2.0",
  "main": [
    { "type": "comment", "text": "--- Typical parameters ---" },
    { "lhs": "TVCL", "rhs": "THETA_CL", "comment": "Typical clearance" },
    { "type": "blank" },
    { "lhs": "CL", "rhs": "TVCL * exp(ETA_CL)" }
  ],
  "ode": [
    { "compartment": "ABS", "rate": "-KA * ABS", "comment": "Absorption depot" },
    { "compartment": "CENTRAL", "rate": "KA * ABS - (CL / VC) * CENTRAL", "comment": "Central compartment" },
    { "type": "blank" },
    { "lhs": "CONC", "rhs": "CENTRAL / VC", "comment": "Plasma concentration" }
  ],
  "f": {
    "ABS": "BIO"
  },
  "lag": {
    "ABS": { "rhs": "0.5", "comment": "Absorption lag" }
  },
  "parameters": [
    { "type": "theta", "name": "BIO", "value": 1.0, "label": "Bioavailability" },
    { "type": "theta", "name": "KA", "value": 1.0, "label": "Absorption rate", "unit": "1/h" },
    { "type": "theta", "name": "VC", "value": 10.0, "label": "Volume of central compartment", "unit": "L" },
    { "type": "theta", "name": "CL", "value": 3.0, "label": "Clearance", "unit": "L/h" },
    { "type": "omega", "name": "KA", "value": 25.0, "var_type": "cv%" },
    { "type": "omega", "name": "VC", "value": 25.0, "var_type": "cv%" },
    { "type": "omega", "name": "CL", "value": 25.0, "var_type": "cv%" }
  ]
}
```

### Loading and Exporting v2.0 JSON Models

You can load a v2.0 JSON model using `CampsisModel()` or `read.campsis()`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
model <- CampsisModel(json = "model_v2.json")
```

To export an existing Campsis model to the structured v2.0 format, specify `version = "2.0"` in `export_to_json()` or `write()`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
model %>% write(file = "model_v2.json", version = "2.0")
```

### Structured Endpoints

Version 2.0 supports structured residual error models (`endpoints`) aligned with `nlmixr2`. The parameterization expects `THETA` parameters holding standard deviations and a unit-variance (`variance = 1`) `SIGMA` parameter.

Supported error model types:
- `additive`: $y = f + a \epsilon$
- `proportional`: $y = f (1 + b \epsilon)$
- `combined1`: $y = f + (a + b f) \epsilon$
- `combined2`: $y = f + \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 f^2} \epsilon$

You can create an endpoint using the `Endpoint()` constructor:

```{r}
endpoint <- Endpoint(
  variable = "CONC",
  error_model = "combined2",
  sigma = "RUV",
  theta_add = "ADD_RUV",
  theta_prop = "PROP_RUV",
  comment = "Observed concentration"
)
endpoint
```

### Simulation Engine Compilation

When exporting a model to simulation engines (`rxode2` or `mrgsolve`), structured endpoints are automatically compiled into their equivalent `[ERROR]` code block representation:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
rx_code <- model %>% export(dest = "rxode2")
```
